Every call in an iii system passes through the engine. Because every worker communicates through the
engine, it can trace work as it moves from one worker to the next, giving you observability across
the whole system without each worker instrumenting itself. The automatically supplied
`iii-observability` worker turns that information into OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs. Do
not declare it in either `config.yaml` or `worker-compose.yaml`.

<Note>
  This page is a quick tour. For the complete configuration and the full list of query functions,
  see the [iii-observability worker docs](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/iii-observability).
</Note>

## Logging

`Logger` from the observability SDK sends each log line of your worker to the engine, so the line
carries the trace and span of the call that logged it. Each level takes a message and optional
structured data.

The examples on this page use a link store: `links::process` appends one link to a store file, and
retries the write.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { appendFile } from "node:fs/promises";
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";
    import { Logger } from "@iii-dev/helpers/observability";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url);

    // without OpenTelemetry, Logger falls back to console.*
    const logger = new Logger();

    type Link = { slug: string; url: string };

    worker.registerFunction("links::process", async (link: Link) => {
      logger.debug("cache lookup", { key: `link:${link.slug}` });

      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 3; attempt += 1) {
        try {
          await appendFile("links.jsonl", `${JSON.stringify(link)}\n`);
          logger.info("processing link", { slug: link.slug, attempt });
          return { slug: link.slug };
        } catch (err) {
          if (attempt === 3) {
            logger.error("failed to persist", { slug: link.slug, err: String(err) });
            throw err;
          }
          logger.warn("retrying write", { attempt });
        }
      }
    });
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    import json
    import os

    from iii import InitOptions, register_worker
    from iii_helpers.observability import Logger

    worker = register_worker(os.environ["III_URL"], InitOptions(worker_name="links"))
    # without OpenTelemetry, Logger falls back to logging, logger iii.logger
    logger = Logger()


    def process_link(link: dict) -> dict:
        logger.debug("cache lookup", {"key": f"link:{link['slug']}"})

        for attempt in range(1, 4):
            try:
                with open("links.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as store:
                    store.write(json.dumps(link) + "\n")
                logger.info("processing link", {"slug": link["slug"], "attempt": attempt})
                return {"slug": link["slug"]}
            except OSError as err:
                if attempt == 3:
                    logger.error("failed to persist", {"slug": link["slug"], "err": str(err)})
                    raise
                logger.warn("retrying write", {"attempt": attempt})
        return {"slug": link["slug"]}


    worker.register_function("links::process", process_link)
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_helpers::observability::Logger;
    use iii_sdk::{Error, InitOptions, RegisterFunction, register_worker};
    use schemars::JsonSchema; // schemars 0.8, the version iii-sdk uses
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use serde_json::json;
    use std::io::Write;

    #[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct Link {
        slug: String,
        url: String,
    }

    #[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct Processed {
        slug: String,
    }

    let url = std::env::var("III_URL").expect("III_URL must be set");
    let worker = register_worker(&url, InitOptions::default());

    worker.register_function(
        "links::process",
        RegisterFunction::new(|link: Link| {
            // without OpenTelemetry, Logger falls back to the `tracing` crate
            let logger = Logger::new();
            let slug = link.slug.clone();
            logger.debug("cache lookup", Some(json!({ "key": format!("link:{slug}") })));

            for attempt in 1..=3 {
                let appended = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
                    .create(true)
                    .append(true)
                    .open("links.jsonl")
                    .and_then(|mut store| writeln!(store, "{}", json!(&link)));

                match appended {
                    Ok(()) => {
                        logger.info(
                            "processing link",
                            Some(json!({ "slug": slug, "attempt": attempt })),
                        );
                        return Ok(Processed { slug });
                    }
                    Err(err) if attempt == 3 => {
                        logger.error(
                            "failed to persist",
                            Some(json!({ "slug": slug, "err": err.to_string() })),
                        );
                        return Err(Error::from(err.to_string()));
                    }
                    Err(_) => logger.warn("retrying write", Some(json!({ "attempt": attempt }))),
                }
            }
            Ok(Processed { slug })
        }),
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
    	"context"
    	"encoding/json"
    	"log"
    	"os"

    	iii "github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii"
    	"github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii/observability"
    )

    type Link struct {
    	Slug string `json:"slug"`
    	URL  string `json:"url"`
    }

    // without OpenTelemetry, Logger falls back to the standard log package
    var logger observability.Logger

    func processLink(ctx context.Context, data json.RawMessage) (any, error) {
    	var link Link
    	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &link); err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}

    	logger.Debug(ctx, "cache lookup", map[string]any{"key": "link:" + link.Slug})

    	for attempt := 1; attempt <= 3; attempt++ {
    		line, err := json.Marshal(link)
    		if err == nil {
    			var store *os.File
    			store, err = os.OpenFile("links.jsonl", os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
    			if err == nil {
    				_, err = store.Write(append(line, '\n'))
    				_ = store.Close()
    			}
    		}
    		if err == nil {
    			logger.Info(ctx, "processing link", map[string]any{"slug": link.Slug, "attempt": attempt})
    			return map[string]any{"slug": link.Slug}, nil
    		}
    		if attempt == 3 {
    			logger.Error(ctx, "failed to persist", map[string]any{"slug": link.Slug, "err": err.Error()})
    			return nil, err
    		}
    		logger.Warn(ctx, "retrying write", map[string]any{"attempt": attempt})
    	}
    	return map[string]any{"slug": link.Slug}, nil
    }

    func main() {
    	client := iii.RegisterWorker(os.Getenv("III_URL"))

    	if _, err := client.RegisterFunction("links::process", processLink); err != nil {
    		log.Fatal(err)
    	}

    	if err := client.Connect(context.Background()); err != nil {
    		log.Fatal(err)
    	}
    	select {}
    }
    ```

### Where the lines go

The engine prints each line in its own output, labeled with the worker's OpenTelemetry service name
(set it with `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`), unless the observability worker sets
`logs_console_output: false`. It also stores each line: `iii call engine::logs::list` returns it,
and the [console](../using-iii/console) shows it next to the trace it was logged in.

Under `iii compose --up`, the engine's output goes to `engine.log` in the compose state directory,
`.iii/compose/<namespace>/` by default (see [Compose logs](../using-iii/compose#compose-logs)).

Before the worker's OpenTelemetry export starts, or when it is off (`OTEL_ENABLED=false`), `Logger`
falls back to the language's own logger, and the line stays in the worker's process.

You can also emit one log line and find it in the stored logs, without a worker:

```bash
# emit a log line
iii call engine::log::info --json '{"message":"processing link"}'

# find it in the stored logs
iii call engine::logs::list | grep -C 10 "processing link"
```

<Note>
  `Logger` does not write to your worker's own output. To print a line in the worker's terminal, use
  the print function of the language.
</Note>

## Traces

A trace captures the spans of a call as it moves across workers, the headline view for debugging a
request end to end. Traces come from worker function invocations: a worker records a span each time
it handles a call. Built-in `engine::*` functions are not traced by default (set
`III_OTEL_TRACE_BUILTINS=true` to include them), so call a worker function to produce a trace. The
Logging examples register `links::process`, a worker function:

```bash
# call the worker function to produce a trace
iii call links::process slug=iii-intro url=https://iii.dev

# count the recorded traces
iii call engine::traces::list | jq '.total'

# print the span tree of the most recent trace
iii call engine::traces::tree trace_id=$(iii call engine::traces::list | jq -r '.traces[-1].trace_id')
```

<Note>
  Traces export on a short delay. If `engine::traces::list` reports `0`, wait a few seconds and call
  `links::process` again.
</Note>

To run a function when a log record or a span is recorded, observe `observability::on-log` or
`observability::on-span`: see [Observers](../using-iii/observers#engine-hosted-event-sources).

## Health and stored data

### Health

```bash
# overall health status
iii call engine::health::check | jq -r .status
```

### Clear stored data

```bash
# clear stored logs
iii call engine::logs::clear

# clear stored traces
iii call engine::traces::clear
```

<Note>
  Logs populate quickly. `engine::logs::clear` followed immediately by `engine::logs::list` can
  still return new logs generated in between the two calls.
</Note>
